text:
A: Hello? Oh, there you are. Can you hear me alright?
B: Yeah. Hiya.
A: Hiya. I'm Joanne. Sorry, I'm never sure if I'm doing these right. Do we just chat?
B: Yeah, that's it really. I'm Gemma.
A: Gemma, okay. I saw your scrubs on the airer in your photo. Are you a nurse?
B: Student. Final year. On an acute medical ward at the minute.
A: Oh, lovely. I'm in care, senior care assistant at a residential home near Huntingdon. Forty beds. I run the day shift, so meds rounds, handovers, the rota, all that.
B: Do you like it?
A: Erm... yeah. Most days. I've just done three twelves on the trot, so ask me again Thursday. I'm knackered. But I'm sort of proud of it, if I'm honest. The day shift runs properly when I'm on. It's the ones who are on their phones all shift that drive me mad.
B: Yeah, we've got a couple of them. HCAs on their phones in the sluice.
A: In the sluice! See, I'd have something to say about that.
B: I did. Got told to soften how I say things. Again.
A: No, that's rubbish, to be honest. If someone's not doing their job, you tell them. I'm the same. Some of the younger ones find me hard work, you know, but the managers don't mind.
B: That's sort of what my mentor says. Good on the hands-on stuff, bad on documentation.
A: Oh, documentation. I keep a paper notebook as well as the electronic records, 'cause I don't trust the system not to go down. It went down for a whole morning in March, and guess who had everything written down.
B: Fair. Our e-obs freezes on nights all the time.
A: There you go. What do you want to do when you qualify, then?
B: Band 5 on a medical ward or A&E. Probably the same trust. Band 6 eventually. Not management.
A: No, I get that. I'm doing my Level 3 leadership diploma, the home's paying for it, 'cause I want deputy manager when ours retires. But not registered manager. No way. I'm worrying weeks before a CQC inspection as it is.
B: What's the diploma like? The writing bits?
A: Erm, it's alright. Slow. I do it on my days off in between batch cooking. Sorry, am I going on?
B: No, it's fine. I've got an essay due Friday I haven't started, so I'm not judging.
A: Friday! Gemma!
B: I know. I always do them the night before.
A: My daughter was like that. Ellie. She's twenty, she's in Peterborough now with her boyfriend.
B: Is that alright?
A: ...Yeah. Sort of. She's an adult, isn't she. You can't tell them. Anyway. Is it London you're in?
B: Catford. One-bed above a dry cleaner's with my husband.
A: Do you get a proper dinner when you get in, or is it toast?
B: Dean does most of the cooking. On nights it's a meal deal and a Twix.
A: Oh, don't. I batch-cook so there's always something in the freezer, otherwise Callum, my son, would live on crisps. He's seventeen. Never puts a plate in the dishwasher, ever.
B: Sounds about right.
A: Do you get much time off, on placement? Do you—
